correctness.rationale: Built the elementary triangular cells directly in 120-degree coordinates on the region -3<=i,j<=2, |i-j|<=2, joined them at shared edges, and exhausted perfect matchings by pairing the first unused triangle with each unused neighbor. This gives 32 triangles, 41 edges, 50 matchings of size 16 and precisely the stated face vector. The planar maps (i,j)->(j,i) and (i,j)->(-1-i,-1-j) give the stated edge permutations; the former exchanges the equal length-two directions. The ordered-pivot computation gives critical dimensions [0,4,4]. On an alternating closed gradient path, the earliest matched stage would insert its pivot. Removing it along a different downward step at that stage is impossible since it would traverse the matched edge backwards; at a later stage both endpoints would still have been available and paired at the earlier stage. This proves acyclicity, and the Morse CW complex has one 0-cell and two 4-cells. For each geometric permutation, independently computed the reduced Euler characteristic of the orbit-face complex by inclusion–exclusion over distinct intersections of projected matching simplices: the orbit counts are 41,23,21,21 and the reduced characteristics 2,-2,0,0. A union of o permutation cycles contributes (-1)^(o-1) to the reduced signed chain trace; the empty face contributes -1. Hopf trace identifies these numbers with the degree-four character, since the other reduced degrees vanish. Decomposition into rational sign representations gives the two stated lines. After barycentric subdivision every simplex stabilizer fixes its simplex pointwise, so quotient chains are coinvariants; in characteristic zero these give invariant homology and group averages yield ranks (0,1,1,0).
residual_risks: The calculation is exact for this graph only. Rational orbit-space homology does not establish integral quotient homology or contractibility.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Rational transfer and character averaging are prior general tools, and mechanically yield quotient ranks once this character is known. The signed fixed-face traces for the actual 2x2x3 geometric maps are the additional information.

evidence: The character, decomposition into sign lines, and rational invariant ranks encode the action on the same H_4, not three independent novelty claims. The exact same-graph indexed character record is the assigned 28ca597615c6 itself.

Side-two records 8108769b07d4 and 5ec127eebc9a give two D6 sign lines in degree three; restricting to the subgroup generated by the half-turn rho^3 and t=rho^3 s0 in their notation gives (2,-2,0,0) in order (1,t,rho^3,t rho^3).
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The abstract character and resulting ranks may coincide for one subgroup on another complex, but the geometric involutions, graph and homological degree here change. value.rationale: This is a natural nonregular neighbor of the standard side-two honeycomb with a known rank-two homology group whose geometric action was not thereby known. The exact signs distinguish its two planar reflections, identify which named quotient retains a class, and give a concrete comparison for future equivariant calculations on honeycomb regions. The contribution is not another tabulation of the ordinary Betti rank.
residual_risks: No general family law, integral representation classification or classification of equivariant homotopy types follows.
